title: The Windows of Heaven
old_p1: The Lord asked His people to pay tithing. Tithing means giving back one part out of every ten to the Lord.
In Malachi’s day, people grew their food. They brought one part to the storehouse. A storehouse was a room for keeping food at the Lord’s house.
The Lord said, “Prove me.” That means, “Try it, and see what I will do.”
old_p2: He promised to “open you the windows of heaven, and pour you out a blessing.” Malachi’s land was dry, so rain from the sky was a big blessing. The Lord pours down blessings like rain.
Children can pay tithing too, one coin out of every ten. Tonight, count three blessings on your fingers before you sleep.
p1: In Malachi's day, families grew much of their own food. They gathered grain and other good things from their fields. The Lord asked them to give Him one part out of every ten. That gift was called tithing.
The food was brought to the Lord's storehouse, where it could be used for His work. Giving a part back was one way the people could show their trust in Him.
p2: Then the Lord made a beautiful promise. He would open the windows of heaven and pour out blessings. Imagine rain falling on dry ground, filling the earth with life. The Lord's blessings can come in many ways, not just as money or things.
Children can give tithing too. If you have ten coins, you can give one back to the Lord. Tonight, count three blessings you are thankful for. Heavenly Father sees your loving choices.
note: Levi, 20 Nov 2026 ("Match up the story lantern stories with the published book"): p1 and p2 are the story words AS PRINTED in the published December book (We Have Waited for Him, on Amazon), first and second story page, word for word, so the Lantern, the app's Books page and the book a family bought read the same. The Christian edition reads God for Heavenly Father; p2_christian only where the printed words are Latter-day Saint teaching. The 29 Oct picture-book rewrite is kept as rewrite_p1/rewrite_p2.
rewrite_p1: In Malachi’s day, people grew their own food. The Lord asked them to pay tithing: one part of every ten, given back.
They brought it to the storehouse, a room for food at the Lord’s house. But many people had stopped bringing it.
So the Lord said, “Prove me.” He meant, “Try it, and see what I will do.”
rewrite_p2: He promised to open “the windows of heaven” and “pour you out a blessing.” Rain falls from the sky and makes food grow. The Lord would pour down blessings like rain, more than they had room for.
Children can pay tithing too, one coin out of every ten. Tonight, count three blessings on your fingers and say thank you.
